title: Talk of AMP bank sale gains traction as CFS speculation mounts
full_text:
Speculation is mounting that plans by AMP to weigh a sale of its bank could be gathering momentum, with talk that the $6bn Australian-listed financial group has been seeking advice from investment banks on what to do with its lender.
A deal to sell the bank could pave a way for a tie-up with Colonial First State, which has previously been speculated. Sources say a sale of the banking business could pay for a transaction. Previously, AMP has always indicated that it would only sell its bank if a buyer was willing to pay at least book value.
Now, some think things could be different, and AMP could be willing to offload the bank at a discount. This is as higher interest rates and a weakening housing market are expected to take a toll on lenders.
The share price has been trading strongly, up 60 per cent in the past year. But the bank is a drag on the group’s capital, and AMP could argue by selling the bank – even at a discount – it could use the cash proceeds to invest in a more profitable business.
A CFS deal is also thought to make strategic sense for AMP, but the question would be how it would fund the transaction.
Shareholders have also previously signalled that they have been averse to mergers and acquisitions.
If the price is discounted, Bendigo Bank would be the obvious buyer, but sources say it has its hands full with integrating the acquisition of the RACQ bank and appeasing APRA in terms of regulatory requirements.
AMP operates one of the country’s leading wealth platforms in North. CFS has the Master Trust investment platform that would be pivotal for AMP in terms of accelerating its position in superannuation and funds administration.
Brookfield, advised by Citi, has been in talks to buy CFS, but the understanding is that work has paused on any potential deal with the owners of CFS – Commonwealth Bank and KKR – and the North American private equity firm a long way apart on price. There has been talk that the asking price is over $5bn.
An option is that AMP and CFS could be merged. KKR purchased 55 per cent of CFS from Commonwealth Bank in 2020 for $1.7bn. A CFS sale process is being run by Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Barrenjoey. For the six months to June, AMP’s bank generated $20m of net profit, down 33.3 per cent on the previous corresponding period.
